The three bands, with the assignments you specified, give **Dq ≈ 1873 cm⁻¹, B ≈ 584 cm⁻¹, C ≈ 2925 cm⁻¹**.

**Method.** I used the term energies (relative to the ³T₁(F) ground) from the d² matrices. The triplet bands depend on Dq and B but not on C, so C is fixed only by the spin-forbidden ¹E band. I linearised the three term energies around a starting point and solved for the three shifts. The result was then checked against the full d² term table.

**Check at Dq = 1873, B = 584, C = 2925:**

| Band | Assignment | Observed (cm⁻¹) | Computed (cm⁻¹) |
|---|---|---|---|
| ν₁ | ³T₂ | 17 500 | 17 479 |
| ν₂ | ³T₁(2) | 25 000 | 24 989 |
| ν₃ | ¹E | 9 748 | 9 745 |

**Caveats.**
- The default fitter (`ts_fit_spectrum`) assigned 9748 cm⁻¹ to the spin-allowed ³T₁→³T₂ transition and gave Dq ≈ 973, B ≈ 1193. That contradicts your assignment, so I did not use it.
- C is determined only through the ¹E band, so its value depends entirely on that assignment. C/B ≈ 5 is high compared with typical values near 4–4.5, which is a further reason to treat C as the least secure number.
- The Dq and B values are the solution of this three-band model under your assignments. A different assignment of the bands would give different parameters.
